search_log.note: Top hits were SELMA3D challenge and chick gastrulation; not cleavage-stage eggs.
S-BIAD865 (genome-wide time-lapse cell division screen, OME-NGFF) is 2D HeLa imaging, not 3D geometry.
Light-sheet embryo projects: idr0068, idr0044, idr0099, idr0118, idr0146, idr0159.
dryad.r4n35 (growth homeostasis, division decoupled from biomass growth) is the only mechanistic hit; none give 3D surface areas.
Loose match; surfaced the Okie Dryad compilation (dryad.t06q9); otherwise clinical IVF reports and figures.

summary: Raw 4D microscopy from which blastomere volume and surface can be segmented is abundant (IDR light-sheet embryo projects such as idr0068 zebrafish and idr0044 mouse; BioImage Archive division time-lapse sets), but no repository dataset was found that already tabulates per-cell surface area and volume before and after division or through egg cleavage; BioNumbers and the Okie Dryad table give only static surface/volume values. The energy-balance clause has no dataset at all.
next_step: Pick one cleavage-stage light-sheet dataset (e.g. an early zebrafish or ascidian embryo in IDR/BIA), segment membranes to get per-blastomere volume and surface for 2–64 cells, and pre-register the surface-increase-at-constant-volume and ratio-restoration test; treat the energetic clause as outside the test.
obstacles_confirmed: Segmentation resolution limits true membrane surface estimates (only raw images are archived, no surface tables).
Geometry alone cannot identify surface-energy balance as the cause of division.
